priceSnapshot.note: THE $63,000 REDUCE RAIL FIRED. After eleven consecutive sessions carrying the same structural line without a single test, the 4H candle covering 07:00-11:00 COT (2026-07-31T12:00-16:00Z) CLOSED at 62,746.1 - a confirmed 4H close below $63,000, exactly the trigger this desk has been pre-committing to since 21 July. The break was not a drift: from the morning snapshot at 63,808.7 price ground sideways for three hours, then dropped 1,335 points in ninety minutes on the heaviest 15m volume of the week (13.17 BTC on the 16:20 COT bar, 490 trades) into a session low of 62,500.0, the lowest print in seventeen days. Price has since recovered 585 points to 63,085.3 and is back above the round number, so the day is now a fight between a confirmed structural break and an equally real reclaim attempt. Session range measured from the morning snapshot is 62,500.0 - 63,833.7, a 2.11% band against a 2.71% daily ATR - three times wider than the 0.71% coil the morning report described.

reduceIf.confirmation: THE FIRST NOTCH IS ALREADY DONE - the $63,000 rail fired on the 11:00 COT 4H close at 62,746.1 and the long-term spot core is being trimmed this session in response, because a rule that is never honoured is not a rule. The rail now moves DOWN to $62,205. The SECOND notch goes if a 4H closes below 62,205, the 1.12M CoinGlass liquidation band that is the single heaviest feature on the entire 48h map. A close through it means the largest pool of forced flow on the chart has been consumed rather than defended, and the next measured shelf behind it is 655.23K at 61,610 - a 2.34% drop from spot with nothing verified in between.

addIf.confirmation: The core only gets rebuilt on a genuine RECLAIM, not on a dip. The trigger is a 4H CLOSE back above $63,282.82 - the 4H EMA200, which had held every single test of this drawdown until today's break and is now the line the market has to win back to cancel the signal. Note the qualifier: CLOSE, not touch. The alternative, cheaper tranche is a tag of the 62,205 magnet that immediately reverses, confirmed by a 15m close back above $62,875 (the measured dead-zone level where liquidation leverage reads exactly 0). Nothing is added while price sits between 62,205 and 63,283 - that band is the vacuum, and buying inside a vacuum is how you get run over.

decisionBox.changed: Four things changed versus this morning, and the first one is the whole report. ONE: the structural rail fired. Eleven sessions of 'watch $63,000' resolved into an actual 4H close at 62,746.1, so the decision box moves from ADD to REDUCE and the paper wallet trims the core rather than adding to it. TWO: price lost the 4H EMA200 at 63,282.82. That average had caught every test of this leg - the morning report explicitly leaned on it to keep a range call alive - and spot at 63,085.3 is now 198 points beneath it. THREE: the liquidation map re-formed a full 1,300 points lower. The 1.16M shelf at 63,529 that the morning report called the dominant feature has been consumed by price; the new dominant band is 1.12M at 62,205.13, and the 0.81% immediately below spot is a MEASURED VACUUM (liquidation leverage reads exactly 0 at both 62,874.82 and 62,577.18). FOUR: the macro backdrop turned genuinely hostile - the US 10-year yield is at 4.748%, a 52-week HIGH, up 7.1bp on the day, while Coinbase reported a $359M quarterly net loss and Strategy an $8.33B operating loss. Bitcoin's two largest listed proxies both missed on the same night the yield curve made a new high.

liquidation.note: THE DOMINANT FEATURE OF THE MAP AND THE REASON THE BEARISH CALL IS NOT YET A CAPITULATION CALL. Liquidation Leverage reads 1.12M on the CoinGlass 48h Model-3 heatmap, taken from the tooltip at the 2026-07-31 11:00 column. The chart's own colour scale tops out at 1.19M, so this is within 6% of the brightest value the surface can display. It sits 1.40% under spot and - critically - 295 points BELOW today's session low of 62,500.0, so the magnet has NOT been tagged yet. It is 5.4x heavier than the largest band above spot (209.25K at 64,511.84). This is where the day's unfinished business is.

655.23K, the second shelf below and 2.34% under spot. This is the level a genuine break of the 62,205 magnet runs to, and it is the arithmetic behind the resting stop at 62,050: that price sits underneath the magnet but comfortably above this shelf, so an ordinary sweep of 62,205 cannot reach it while a real breakdown will.

MEASURED VACUUM: Liquidation Leverage reads exactly 0 at this price, 0.33% under spot. Read together with the 62,577.18 reading below, the entire 0.33%-0.81% band beneath the market is empty. That is the mechanical argument for why this morning's slide travelled 1,335 points in ninety minutes rather than grinding, and why a second probe lower would move just as fast.

Also exactly 0, 0.81% under spot and just above the 62,500.0 session low. Two independent zero readings between spot and the 62,205 magnet mean there is nothing for price to grab on the way in. It also doubles as the confirmation line for a reclaim: a 15m close back above 62,875 after a magnet tag is the only add trigger this report will accept below 63,283.

59.63K, the nearest band above spot at +0.85%. Effectively nothing - it is 1/19th the weight of the magnet below - and it sits just under the 1H EMA20 at 63,699. A bounce meets no meaningful liquidation resistance here, which is why the reclaim trigger is set at the 4H EMA200 (63,283) rather than at a heatmap level: above spot the map is too thin to define anything.

53.97K, 1.55% above spot and marginally lighter than the band beneath it. The 15m EMA200 sits at 64,056.43 and the 1h EMA50 at 64,033.99, so 64,030-64,065 is a technical shelf with no liquidation weight behind it.

209.25K, 2.26% above spot - the first band above the market with real weight, and still only 19% of the magnet below. It sits just under the 1H EMA200 (64,513.01) to within two dollars, which makes 64,510-64,515 the single most confluent resistance on the chart and a realistic upper bound for any relief rally that does not change the regime.

liquidityMagnet.note: The pull is DOWN and the imbalance is wider than it was this morning. 1.12M sitting 1.40% below spot against 59.63K immediately above and 209.25K at the first meaningful band above is a 5.4:1 skew toward the downside on the heaviest reading. Read this as gravity, not prophecy: the magnet says where forced flow sits, and today's session low of 62,500.0 stopped 295 points short of it, which is unfinished business rather than a completed move.

atr.source: Computed here (Wilder ATR-14) from Kraken XBTUSDT daily OHLC over 45 sessions through the in-progress 2026-07-31 UTC candle, seeded on a 14-bar simple average of true range then Wilder-smoothed. Math: TR = max(H-L, |H-Cprev|, |L-Cprev|), then ATR = (ATRprev x 13 + TR) / 14. ATR has EXPANDED sharply again, from the morning's 1,633.93 to 1,707.49 (+4.5%), because the in-progress daily candle has now covered 65,388.0 - 62,500.0 = $2,888, nearly double the completed 2026-07-30 range of $1,541. At 2.71% of spot a normal day now covers about $1,707. That is the number behind the resting stop at 62,050: it is $1,035 below spot, roughly six tenths of an ATR, and it sits below the 62,205 magnet but above the 61,610 shelf.

timeframes.structure: THE FRAME THAT FLIPPED, AND THE REASON THIS REPORT IS NO LONGER A RANGE CALL. Six hours ago the 4H was the anchor of the range thesis: price sat above the EMA200 at 63,392.77 with a fractionally POSITIVE MACD histogram of +5.69. Both of those are gone. The EMA200 now reads 63,282.82 and price at 63,085.3 is 198 points BENEATH it, the first time this drawdown has lost it. All four EMAs are now above price and the 20/50/100 cluster at 64,030-64,309 is a thick ceiling. A 4H close back above 63,282.82 is the only thing that repairs this.

earnings.note: Coinbase reported a Q2 net loss of $359 million, or -$1.36 per share, against a consensus of -$0.01, on revenue of $1.2 billion that missed by roughly $150 million. The stock fell about 6.5% after hours to $152.90 on Thursday and was down a further 9.6% on MarketWatch's live trending-tickers strip at 12:45 COT today. Bright spots existed - a record 10.3% trading-volume market share and subscription revenue at 48% of net revenue - but a loss that large from the sector's flagship listed exchange is a direct read on retail activity, and it is one of the two named catalysts behind today's break.

Strategy posted an $8.33 billion Q2 operating loss, almost entirely an $8.32 billion unrealised mark-down on its Bitcoin holdings, with revenue of $122 million against $124.5 million expected and EPS of -$24.45 against +$3.07 expected. The shares closed Thursday up 4.73% but traded down after hours. The number matters less as a corporate result than as a reflexivity signal: the largest corporate holder is now printing eight-figure-per-day paper losses, which raises the market's perceived probability of forced or discretionary supply from the one buyer that has been price-insensitive for two years.

calibration.rollingRecord: ELEVEN consecutive sessions with the $63,000 structural reduce rail set, and on session ELEVEN it fired: the 4H candle covering 07:00-11:00 COT closed at 62,746.1, and the session low of 62,500.0 is the lowest print in seventeen days. Session-by-session since yesterday morning: morning range-bull 34/44/22 at 64,821.4, midday range-bull 35/45/20 at 64,941.6, endday range-bear 28/45/27 at 64,763.2, midnight range-bear 23/44/33 at 64,050.0, morning range-bear 23/42/35 at 63,808.7, and this report bearish 22/33/45 at 63,085.3. That is four consecutive sessions of rising bearish weight into a break that then happened - the direction was called correctly and progressively, session after session.
calibration.note: actingHelped is FALSE, and the reason is worth being blunt about. The morning read the direction right - it wrote that the pull was down, that a probe lower would travel fast through the dead zone, and it kept the bearish tilt - and then took the OPPOSITE action, deploying a 6 USDT spot DCA at 63,808.7 on the strength of an Extreme Fear print of 25 and a +$233M ETF inflow day. That tranche is down 1.13%. It also explicitly declined the short, and the short would have paid: the trade it described but did not take (short toward the magnet) would have covered the 1,335-point slide. The loss is trivial in dollars - roughly 7 cents on 6 USDT - but the error is not trivial in kind: the report and the trade pointed in opposite directions. The morning's stated stop of 63,200 was also violated on the way to 62,500, which is the second failure to note. The correction this session is to make the trade agree with the analysis: the rail fired, so the core gets trimmed.
